router_body:
name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: full job set selected
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: echo 'SELECTED gate tier'
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
      - name: local gate wiring proof
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: python3 -I ci/local-gate-test.py
      - name: local evidence gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix')) }}
        run: echo 'Local gauntlet evidence is the gate; request ci or full-matrix for CI.'

ci.yml.gate:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: {node-version: '22'}

      - name: install tree-sitter-cli (pinned by lockfile)
        run: npm ci

      # Gate 1: the committed generated parser is in sync with grammar.js.
      # src/parser.c is committed on purpose — Helix's `hx -g build` and
      # Zed's extension builder compile it straight from the repo and
      # never run `tree-sitter generate` themselves.
      - name: generated parser current
        run: |
          npx tree-sitter generate
          git diff --exit-code -- src/

      # Gate 2: the grammar's own corpus (test/corpus/*.txt).
      - name: corpus tests
        run: npx tree-sitter test

      # Gate 3: the three query files load against the grammar.
      - name: queries load
        run: |
          printf 'fn main() -> !int {\n    print("hi, {who:>8}")\n    0\n}\n' > /tmp/q.lu
          for q in highlights locals injections; do
            npx tree-sitter query "queries/$q.scm" /tmp/q.lu --test >/dev/null
          done

      # Gate 4: wolf-lang's full corpus parses at ZERO ERROR nodes.
      # The only exclusions are the corpus's own parse-tier
      # counter-examples (`check: fail(E00xx|E01xx|E02xx)` directives) —
      # files the spec itself says do not parse.
      - name: checkout wolf-lang corpus
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          repository: wolffe-lang/wolf-lang
          path: .wolf-lang
          sparse-checkout: corpus

      - name: wolf-lang corpus at zero ERRORs
        run: TREE_SITTER="npx tree-sitter" sh script/parse-wolf-corpus.sh .wolf-lang/corpus

  # The schedule above SLEEPS after 60 days without repository activity
  # (#12), and a sleeping schedule is silent: no run, so no red, so no
  # `notify`. This job is the red that comes before the silence.
  #
  # Why an alarm and not a keepalive. The two keepalive shapes are a bot
  # commit on a cron, and a scheduled step calling the REST `enable`
  # endpoint on its own workflow so the timer never fires. The first
  # writes noise into a mirror's history. The second was the DEFAULT
  # mode of gautamkrishnar/keepalive-workflow v2, and GitHub Staff
  # disabled that repository for a terms-of-service violation; the
  # reason reported downstream (ddev/github-action-add-on-test#46) is
  # that it circumvented the 60-day inactivity policy. Both shapes exist
  # to defeat the timer, so both put this org's Actions at risk for a
  # daily corpus check. The timer is GitHub's to run. What this repo
  # owes is that nobody is SURPRISED by it.
  #
  # So: every scheduled run reads the default branch's last commit date
  # and, at 45 days (15 daily runs before the 60-day cliff), goes red
  # and opens one issue naming the date the schedule sleeps. A human
  # then chooses: land something real, or let it sleep and press
  # "Enable workflow" (`gh workflow enable ci.yml`) when wanted. It
  # changes no workflow state and writes nothing to git.
  #
  # "Activity" is not defined by GitHub's docs. The last trunk COMMIT is
  # the conservative reading: a commit is certainly activity, and a
  # fast-forwarded commit's committer date predates its push, so the
  # alarm can only fire early, never late. The run log also prints each
  # workflow's `state` from the API, so the log says whether the
  # platform already put one to sleep.
ci.yml.sleep-alarm:
if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: days until the schedule sleeps
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          WARN_DAYS: ${{ inputs.sleep_warn_days || '45' }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$WARN_DAYS" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "::error::sleep_warn_days must be a whole number, got '$WARN_DAYS'"; exit 2 ;; esac
          branch=$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .default_branch)
          last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits?sha=$branch&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].commit.committer.date')
          test -n "$last"
          last_s=$(date -u -d "$last" +%s)
          age=$(( ( $(date -u +%s) - last_s ) / 86400 ))
          sleeps=$(date -u -d "@$(( last_s + 60 * 86400 ))" +%Y-%m-%d)
          echo "workflow states (API):"
          gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows" --jq '.workflows[] | "  \(.path)  \(.state)"'
          echo "last $branch commit: $last ($age day(s) ago); schedules sleep on or after $sleeps; alarm at $WARN_DAYS day(s)"
          if [ "$age" -lt "$WARN_DAYS" ]; then
            echo "quiet: $(( WARN_DAYS - age )) day(s) before the alarm"
            exit 0
          fi
          MARKER='scheduled gate will sleep'
          BODY=$(printf '%s\n\n- run: %s\n- last `%s` commit: %s (%s days ago)\n- alarm threshold: %s days\n\nGitHub disables this repository'"'"'s scheduled workflows after 60 days without activity, and a disabled schedule never runs, so it never goes red (#12). Either land a real change on `%s`, or let the schedule sleep and re-enable it with `gh workflow enable ci.yml --repo %s` when it is wanted again. No bot keeps it awake, on purpose: see the `sleep-alarm` comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.\n' \
            "The scheduled corpus gate sleeps on or after $sleeps." "$RUN_URL" "$branch" "$last" "$age" "$WARN_DAYS" "$branch" "$REPO")
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open \
            --search "in:title \"$MARKER\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$BODY"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" \
              --title "CI: $MARKER on or after $sleeps" --body "$BODY"
          fi
          echo "::error::$age day(s) since the last $branch commit; the schedule sleeps on or after $sleeps"
          exit 1

  # A red that nobody is looking at is not a gate either. The scheduled
  # fire above runs when no human is watching by construction, so the
  # red has to come and find one: this job opens an issue (or comments
  # on the one already open) naming the run.
  #
  # Deliberately NOT run for `pull_request` or `push`: those reds
  # already have a human attached to them, and filing an issue for
  # every red PR would train everyone to ignore the label.
  #
  # Idempotent: one issue per outage, not one per day. It searches for
  # an open issue carrying the marker below and comments if it finds
  # one, so a break that stays broken for a week is one thread with
  # seven comments, and closing the issue by hand is what resets it.
ci.yml.notify:
needs: gate
    if: >-
      failure() && (
        github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
        github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch' ||
        github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      )
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: open or update the red-CI issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          # The marker is the search key; keep it verbatim in the title.
          MARKER='unattended CI run is red'
          BODY=$(printf '%s\n\n- run: %s\n- trigger: `%s`\n- gated input: wolf-lang default branch (this repo may have had no commits)\n\nThe corpus gate reads wolf-lang'"'"'s default branch, so the likely cause is an upstream surface change this grammar has not mirrored yet. `script/parse-wolf-corpus.sh` names the failing files in the run log.\n' \
            "The $EVENT run of CI failed on $REPO." "$RUN_URL" "$EVENT")
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open \
            --search "in:title \"$MARKER\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            echo "commenting on existing #$existing"
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$BODY"
          else
            echo "opening a new issue"
            # tl28 (ruling #92): every repository's unattended red carries
            # one label, so the next lane on it can find what it owes. The
            # label may exist already; that is not a failure.
            gh label create nightly-red --repo "$REPO" --color B60205 \
              --description "a scheduled run on trunk is red; the next lane on the repo owes it" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" \
              --title "CI: $MARKER ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))" \
              --label nightly-red \
              --body "$BODY"
          fi

  # The run's verdict, and its name: `tier full`, this repository's one
  # tier. It needs the gate, runs unless the run was cancelled, proves the
  # wiring first (ci/tiers-test.py) and fails unless every job it needs
  # succeeded (ci/tiers.py verdict). lane-audit.sh reads its name and
  # conclusion. (`sleep-alarm` and `notify` are the schedule's, not the
  # tier's: they run on their own conditions, as before.)
ci.yml.tier:
name: tier full
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [gate]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: the wiring can say no (ci/tiers-test.py)
        run: python3 ci/tiers-test.py
      - name: every job succeeded
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict
